start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-observations-and-their-corrections with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and observations [{\"id\": \"walk-2026-11-17\", \"observed_at\": \"2026-11-17T18:00:00Z\", \"about\": \"walk\", \"values\": [{\"name\": \"steps\", \"amount\": 6000, \"unit\": \"count\"}], \"source\": \"typed by me\"}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the entries are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-observations-and-their-corrections" with store and, when you have them, the observations to keep.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example entries: the prove step must give every expected answer, or the run stops and says which.

4. Every later run keeps the new observations and later words (confirm, discard, correct, merge) as their own entries and reads each one back; ask your AI what is current, what waits for a word or how one value went over time, and it reads the store's own objects.
